newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's AMI Insurance year profit falls to NZ$5.9 mln.
newsitem.headline: NZ's AMI Insurance year profit falls to NZ$5.9 mln.

text.p: AMI Insurance on Monday reported an after-tax profit of NZ$5.9 million for the year to June 30, down from $9.8 million a year earlier.
AMI said the drop in profit reflected its board's philosophy that benefits should be returned to policyholders through improved policy features.

"Expenses were held to an increase of only 1.8 percent, but the cost of claims increased by 9.1 percent. While following the industry trend, the cost of claims increase was well below the industry's experience of 13 percent for a product range similar to AMI's," AMI said.
"Written premiums of $137.5 million were relatively static, reflecting the board's decision to defer premium increases to May 1996 despite the increasing cost of claims."
AMI said its reserves had been increased by nearly 10 percent to $76.5 million and the solvency margin rose to 56.6 percent from 51.8 percent.
Investment income was up by a record 42 percent to $11.9 million and assets reached a five-year record of $149.1 million.
AMI said the increasing rate of insurance fraud and crime was an emerging issue for the industry.

"Estimates suggest that these acts against insurers could be costing the industry up to $50 million a year. The phenomenon is not new, but the increasing incidence of deliberate and organised fraud is of real concern," AMI said.
AMI's annual meeting will be held in Christchurch on December 18. -- Wellington newsroom (64 4) 473 4746
